title: Sell Mineral Rights in Cheyenne, WY
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Cheyenne, WY | Laramie County
metaDescription: Cheyenne sits on the checkerboard and near the DJ Basin's northern reach. Get a courthouse-grounded, honest read on your Laramie County mineral interest.
heroLead: Cheyenne carries two separate mineral stories at once, the Union Pacific checkerboard that runs the length of the old transcontinental corridor, and the DJ Basin's Niobrara trend reaching up from Colorado. Which one applies to you depends entirely on your section.
intro: As the state capital and the seat of Laramie County, Cheyenne also sits at a genuine geologic crossroads. The railroad checkerboard, alternating sections granted to the Union Pacific back in the 1860s, runs through this whole corridor, meaning some land here carries clean private mineral ownership while adjacent sections stayed federal, BLM-administered ground. Separately, the productive Niobrara and Codell intervals that built the Silo Field extend up from Colorado into eastern Laramie County.

Before I say anything about your mineral interest, I need to know which story it belongs to, or possibly both, since I've seen tracts here with checkerboard-pattern ownership sitting directly over active DJ Basin leasing.

sections.heading: Reading the checkerboard around Cheyenne
paragraphs: Odd-numbered sections along the old Union Pacific right-of-way were patented to the railroad and later sold into private hands, often with minerals included. Even sections generally remained federal. That pattern still shows up clearly on modern plat maps around Cheyenne, and it directly determines whether your family holds a private asset you can sell outright, or whether the minerals under your description are federally owned and administered through BLM leasing instead.
I check this first for every Laramie County tract, because it changes the entire conversation about what, if anything, is actually yours to sell.

sections.heading: DJ Basin activity reaching the capital
paragraphs: Eastern Laramie County has seen real horizontal Niobrara and Codell development tied to the broader Silo Field trend, and Cheyenne's outskirts fall within that footprint in places. A tract with both private checkerboard ownership and active DJ Basin leasing nearby can carry genuine, current value beyond what raw undeveloped acreage would command.

sections.heading: Confirming your specific situation
paragraphs: I pull the Laramie County recorder's records for your exact legal description, confirm whether your section is a private railroad-grant tract or federal ground, and check current lease and unit status. That combination tells me the real picture before I quote you anything.

faqs.question: How do I know if my land is on the checkerboard?
faqs.answer: Send me your legal description and I'll check whether your section historically traces to a Union Pacific land grant.

faqs.question: Is Cheyenne part of the same play as Colorado's Wattenberg field?
faqs.answer: Related, same Niobrara and Codell target formations, but the northern DJ Basin here produces differently than the denser Colorado development.

faqs.question: What if my minerals are federally owned?
faqs.answer: Federal minerals aren't privately sellable in the same way. I'll clarify whether your specific interest is private or federal before we go further.

faqs.question: Does being the state capital change anything about my mineral rights?
faqs.answer: No direct effect. Cheyenne's status as capital doesn't change the underlying mineral ownership or geology, only where the county recorder's office happens to sit.
